person: Walt Brenner is 66 and runs a 24-person surveying and renovation firm, Brenner Field Services, with crews in three states. His part-time bookkeeper sends out the firm's invoices, but a few commercial customers make him use their payment websites, and he does not know what happens after an invoice goes in. Several invoices are unpaid, and one customer paid less than the invoice with no explanation. He wants to know what is owed, what is not owed, and what it costs him to push. He prints anything long and distrusts anything that seems to be selling him something.
stated_up_front: I am not a computer person. I have some invoices that never got paid, a couple of them through those customer websites, and I want to know which ones I am really owed and what to do about it. Tell me in plain words and big print, and don't send anything to anybody without asking me.

facts.truth: Five: Harlow County Schools (Coupa), Delmar Properties and Ridgeway Builders (Ariba), Cobalt Title (Bill.com portal), and Sam Tillery, a homeowner who pays by emailed invoice.
Invoice 2291 for $6,400 was rejected in Coupa. Walt thinks it was something about the purchase order but has not read the comment.
Invoice 2304 for $9,800 shows payment scheduled for 120 days out. Walt remembers the contract saying 30 days.
Invoice 2287 for $5,250 still says pending in Ariba, but Walt thinks the check cleared at Chase around October 6.

facts.about: Cobalt Title on the Bill.com portal
facts.truth: Invoice 2296 for $3,100 is on hold. Walt thinks it is about a tax form but does not know whose.
Invoice 2279 was $2,000. Sam paid $1,500 and the Chase memo says 'delay credit'. The contract has a late-finish credit.
Invoice 2310 for $4,000 was approved in Coupa on October 15 and is not due yet.
Two jobs for Cobalt this year, a $3,100 survey and an earlier $1,200 one, so about $4,300 together.
Signed contracts are in a blue filing cabinet at the office, and the payroll stub has his EIN. The bookkeeper is Denise, part-time on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
He invoices as Brenner Field Services LLC, based in New York.

unknowns: Whether the New York freelancer law applies to any of these jobs
What the Coupa rejection comment actually says
Whether the W-9 on file with Cobalt is the current one
What the late-finish credit allows Sam to keep
